route_A_conditions: A1 IMPORT UNEDITED, PINNED: each original is imported as it stands; its blob and sha256-lf16 are printed and checked at launch against the pins the READY records (the blob that produced the recorded headline where the record names one; otherwise the blob at the READY, with C0 as the witness)

A2 THE REDIRECT: sqlite3.connect is wrapped FOR THE DURATION OF THAT CONSUMER'S CALL ONLY; every open, whatever the original asked for, becomes file:<absolute path>?mode=ro&immutable=1 AFTER the -wal / -journal emptiness check (a non-empty one refuses: a failed precondition); the connection log (path, URI, count) is printed per consumer; the wrapper is removed after the call

A3 NO WRITE CAN LAND: the redirected connections are read-only and immutable, so any real write (INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE, a CREATE of a MISSING table, a committed change) raises and the consumer's cell is UNDETERMINED (BY VALIDITY); a CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on an EXISTING table and a no-op commit are admitted only because they write nothing; sha256_16, size and mtime of every opened file are asserted unchanged after each consumer

A4 ZERO CALLS, ENFORCED: each consumer runs with every judge API key removed from its environment and a socket guard that refuses any outbound connection; a cache miss therefore REFUSES instead of posting; the run's call count is printed (must be 0)

A5 ONE SUBPROCESS PER CONSUMER: the CERT cell (which stubs stack_judge) and every original run in separate processes, so no stub, monkeypatch or module state is shared; STACK, STACK-v2 and LEAF-POWERED import the REAL stack_judge only inside their own redirected subprocess

A6 THE HEADLINE IS CAPTURED FROM THE ORIGINAL'S OWN COMPUTATION (its return value, or its printed headline parsed by a pinned pattern that the READY reviews), never re-implemented; the removal is applied to the original's INPUT (its verdict rows / scored set), never to its code

A7 C0 IS THE EXECUTION WITNESS: the recorded headline must reproduce TO THE DIGIT through the redirect before any removal; a consumer that does not is UNDETERMINED (BY VALIDITY) and excluded, the others proceed; the READY includes a NEGATIVE CONTROL showing the redirect refuses a real write (a synthetic original that INSERTs) and a missing-table CREATE

plain_description.what: For 13 recorded results that used questions whose near-duplicate copies leaked into the construction side, removes the exposed questions and re-scores each result. Each shift is compared with removing the same number of random questions from the same subjects (no judge calls).
plain_description.why: Questions were split by id rather than by content, so some copies leaked. This measures whether the leak moved the results, to inform the author's rebuild-or-disclose decision (it decides nothing itself).
plain_description.information: Shifts no larger than random removals would mean the leak did not change results. Larger shifts would point to contamination. Result: on 12 of 13 results the shift is within random variation. One certificate-filter readout moved unusually: around the 99th percentile at the registered random stream, but only about the 90th when averaged over several streams. One flag in 13 is what chance gives about half the time. No recorded verdict changes, and this does not prove that no leak mechanism exists. It re-scores results on the older question pool, which is now ruled history, not evidence.
